label: Jeremiah

text.BHSA NEH 12:11: וְיֹויָדָע֙ הֹולִ֣יד אֶת־יֹונָתָ֔ן וְיֹונָתָ֖ן הֹולִ֥יד אֶת־יַדּֽוּעַ׃
text.KJV NEH 12:11: And Joiada begat Jonathan, and Jonathan begat Jaddua.
text.BHSA NEH 12:12: וּבִימֵי֙ יֹֽויָקִ֔ים הָי֥וּ כֹהֲנִ֖ים רָאשֵׁ֣י הָאָבֹ֑ות לִשְׂרָיָ֣ה מְרָיָ֔ה לְיִרְמְיָ֖ה חֲנַנְיָֽה׃
text.KJV NEH 12:12: And in the days of Joiakim were priests, the chief of the fathers: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;
text.KJV NEH 12:13: Of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;

A.name: Jeremiah
A.notes: named on the sealed document of NEH 10:1-27 (NEH 10:2)
family: companion-of zerubbabel-2 (Zerubbabel, returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity (EZR 2:2, N)
companion-of jeshua-3 (Jeshua, returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity (EZR 2:2, N)
descendant-of aaron (Aaron, brother of Moses (EXO 4:14) and Levitical priest (EXO 28:1))

B.name: Jeremiah
B.line: Priestly family head from Zerubbabel's return, continuing under Joiakim
family: companion-of zerubbabel-2 (Zerubbabel, returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity (EZR 2:2, N)
companion-of jeshua-3 (Jeshua, returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity (EZR 2:2, N)

why: The Hebrew לְיִרְמְיָה חֲנַנְיָה identifies Hananiah as head of Jeremiah’s priestly house in Joiakim’s days, matching B’s stated role. A shares the same relevant ancestry links, however, so the verse alone does not firmly distinguish the records.
